memory_leads.lead: Container shipping remained structurally oversupplied after the pre-2008 order boom; carriers pursued ever-larger ships, slow steaming, cost cutting and alliance/network cooperation while freight rates were often weak and volatile.

The industry moved through several alliance configurations before converging into 2M, Ocean Alliance and THE Alliance structures, reflecting scale economics and the need to fill mega-ships across global networks.
Hanjin Shipping's collapse became a major operational and credit shock, stranding cargo and highlighting financial fragility in liner shipping.
unknowns: How quickly counterparties repriced carrier credit risk

memory_leads.lead: A major consolidation wave reduced the number of global liner carriers through acquisitions and mergers; examples in model memory include Maersk/Hamburg Süd, COSCO/OOCL, Hapag-Lloyd/UASC and the creation of ONE from Japanese liner businesses.
Ultra-large container vessels expanded rapidly, particularly on Asia-Europe routes, lowering nominal slot cost while increasing port/terminal and network concentration requirements.

Dry bulk suffered a long post-supercycle hangover as fleet deliveries met slower commodity growth; the 2015-2016 period appears to have included historically depressed earnings and distressed asset values.
European shipping banks retrenched, German KG financing contracted sharply, and alternative capital entered through private equity, public equity, Chinese leasing and sale-leaseback structures.

China and South Korea became dominant shipbuilding centers with Japan still significant; persistent yard overcapacity led to restructurings, closures and consolidation, while high-value LNG and specialized vessels favored technically stronger yards.
unknowns: Country order shares by vessel type

memory_leads.lead: Tanker markets cycled through crude/product demand changes, refinery shifts, sanctions and fleet growth; low oil prices after 2014 and occasional floating-storage/arbitrage conditions affected tonne-miles and earnings.

LNG shipping moved toward a much larger and more flexible market as U.S., Australian and other liquefaction projects expanded, spot/portfolio trading grew and modern dual-fuel vessels displaced older steam designs.

IMO efficiency and emissions regulation accelerated through EEDI, the Ballast Water regime and the approaching 2020 global sulfur cap, creating major uncertainty over scrubbers, compliant fuel and fleet-renewal economics.

IMO 2020 preparation became a central cross-segment decision: install scrubbers, burn low-sulfur fuel, use LNG fuel, or retire inefficient tonnage; expectations depended heavily on the future high-sulfur/low-sulfur fuel spread.

Container terminals became larger and more automated, with increasing crane reach, yard automation and appointment/digital systems, while mega-ships produced larger call-size peaks and landside congestion challenges.
Somali piracy declined after coordinated naval/security measures, while other security risks including West African piracy, sanctions and chokepoint tensions remained relevant.
U.S.-China trade tensions created uncertainty over container volumes, sourcing shifts and dry-bulk/agricultural trade routes before the pandemic shock arrived.
unknowns: Carrier guidance and shipper sourcing judgments

judgment_leads.judgment: Many liner participants likely believed mega-ships and alliances were necessary to restore unit-cost competitiveness, even while industry-wide ordering risked perpetuating oversupply.
judgment_leads.outcome_boundary: Separate firm-level cost logic from system-wide capacity outcomes.

judgment_leads.judgment: Dry-bulk owners and investors debated whether distressed asset prices represented a generational buying opportunity or a prolonged structural oversupply trap.
judgment_leads.outcome_boundary: Do not use later recoveries to overwrite the uncertainty.

judgment_leads.judgment: Hanjin's failure likely shifted expectations toward faster liner consolidation and greater emphasis on counterparty reliability.
judgment_leads.outcome_boundary: Verify which views were contemporaneous rather than later narrative.

judgment_leads.judgment: IMO 2020 created divergent investment theses around scrubber payback, fuel spreads and accelerated scrapping of older ships.
judgment_leads.outcome_boundary: Later realized fuel spreads cannot be used as if known in 2019.
